title: Isoperimetry from regular averaged indicators
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and suppose its standard Gaussian measure has real value $\alpha\in(0,1)$. For every $u\in(0,\pi/2)$, define $f_u(x)=\int 1_A(\cos(u)x+\sin(u)y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. Suppose that for each such $u$ there are a continuous-linear-functional-valued map $D_u$, a constant $C_u\ge0$, and a real number $M_u$ such that $D_u(x)$ is the derivative of $f_u$ at every $x$, $D_u$ is globally Lipschitz with constant $C_u$, and $\|D_u(x)\|\le M_u$ for every $x$. Then the Gaussian profile $U(\alpha)$, converted to an extended nonnegative real, is at most the Gaussian surface area of $A$, defined by the lower limit of its scaled rotation sensitivities as the angle tends to zero from above.
hypotheses_covered: The standard Gaussian measure of $A$ has real value $\alpha$
For each such $u$, $D_u(x)$ is the derivative of the averaged indicator at every $x$
For each such $u$, $D_u$ is globally Lipschitz with constant $C_u\ge0$
For each such $u$, there is a real $M_u$ bounding $\|D_u(x)\|$ for all $x$
replaced: Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. Write $P_\gamma(A)=\liminf_{t\to0^+}\bigl[\sqrt{\pi/2}\,s_A(t)/t\bigr]_+$ in $[0,\infty]$, where $[x]_+=\max(x,0)$. Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable with $\gamma_n(A)=\alpha\in(0,1)$ and put $f_u(x)=\mathbb E[\mathbf1_A(\cos u\,x+\sin u\,G)]$. Suppose that for each $0<u<\pi/2$, $f_u$ has a derivative family $D_u$ and there exist constants $C_u\ge0$ and $M_u\in\mathbb R$ such that $D_u$ is $C_u$-Lipschitz and $\|D_u(x)\|\le M_u$ for all $x$. Then $\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(\alpha))\le P_\gamma(A)$, where $\varphi$ and $\Phi$ are the standard Gaussian density and distribution function.
